title: Checkpoint: World 1
objectives: Apply everything learned in World 1 (variables, data types, assignment, operators, input/output, constants, swapping) together

hook.text: You have reached the end of World 1. Now it is time to test everything you have learned with mixed questions.

concept.heading: Checkpoint
concept.body: This lesson does not teach a new topic; it reinforces what you have learned. The questions below test variables, data types, assignment, operators, input/output, constants, and swapping in a mix.

exercises.question: What data type is the value "25"?

feedback.correct: Correct. A number with no decimal part: an integer.
feedback.incorrect: 25 has no decimal part, so it is an integer.

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
Put the setup steps (the READ and assignment part) in the correct order before printing the larger of two numbers entered by the user.
When a ← 5 and b ← 9, what should the first step be to swap their values?

feedback.correct: Correct. The value of a must be saved into temp before it is lost.
feedback.incorrect: The first step of a swap is to save the value of a into a temporary variable.

exercises.question: With CONST TAX ← 0.10, what does this code write to the screen?
Which of these is NOT a valid variable name?

feedback.correct: Correct. A variable name cannot start with a digit.
feedback.incorrect: "2number" is invalid because it starts with a digit; names must start with a letter.

exercises.question: Which data type is used to store whether a student passed the course (yes or no)?

feedback.correct: Correct. The boolean type is used for information with only two states.
feedback.incorrect: Two-state information like yes or no is stored as a boolean (TRUE/FALSE).

summary: World 1 complete: variables, data types, assignment, operators, input/output, constants, and swapping.
These concepts form the foundation of decisions and loops from World 2 onward.
You will see the topics you struggled with again in your review queue.
